I have been farming these 4.5 mu in Quzhou County for 45 years. I never went to school, so everything I know comes from working the land with my own hands and watching what the neighbors do. Last year I grew Bt cotton — the improved seeds that Old Zhang from the east end of the village used. His crop had fewer worms than mine the year before, so I will buy the same seeds again from the dealer. I plant in the spring, around the end of April when the soil gets warm.

For fertilizer, I do the same as last year. I will buy three 50-kilogram bags of compound fertilizer, the kind that says 15-15-15 on the bag. I spread this on the field before planting — that works out to a little over one bag for every 1.5 mu. Then when the cotton starts flowering and again when the bolls are forming, I topdress with urea. I use two 50-kilogram bags of urea for the whole plot, half a bag each time. I know potassium is good for cotton, but the compound fertilizer already has some, and buying extra potassium costs too much. I would rather put that money into pesticide, because worms can destroy the whole crop, but a little less fertilizer only means a slightly smaller harvest.

I irrigate three times from my well: once right after planting to help the seeds sprout, once when the plants flower, and once when the bolls are getting fat. My neighbor waters four times, but his electricity bill is too high and my well pump is old. Three times has been enough for me.

Cotton needs a lot of spraying. I spray pesticide ten times this year. I start when the seedlings come up and then keep spraying every couple of weeks, or whenever I see bollworms or aphids. Everyone around here sprays about this much. If you skip even one spray, the worms will eat you out of house and home.

I till the soil with a rotary machine. I hire the tractor for half a day because my back is not what it used to be.

I expect about 95 kilograms of lint cotton per mu if the weather is decent. Last year I got around 90 because it was too dry, so this year I will make sure to water well at flowering time. I have only 4.5 mu, so every yuan counts, but a bad harvest is worse than wasting a bit of fertilizer.
